General Description
Choloramphenicol

Chloramphenicol is a representative broad-spectrum antibiotic.
Chloramphenicol (oily injection) is a complementary drug.
Capsules, chloramphenicol 250 mg.
Chloramphenicol (as palmitate) 125mg/5ml oral suspension 60ml.
Injection (powder for solution for injection), chloramphenicol (as sodium succinate) 1-g vial.
Oily injection (suspension for injection), chloramphenicol (as sodium succinate) 250 mg/ml, 2-ml ampoule.

Guidelines for use
Severe life-threatening infections, particularly those caused by haemophilus influenzae, and typhoid fever; also cerebral abscess; mastoiditis; relapsing fever; gangrene; granuloma inguinale; listeriosis; severe melioidosis; plague; psitticosis; tularaemia; Whipple disease; septicaemia; empirical treatment of meningitis.

Contraindications:
Pregnancy; breastfeeding; porphyria.

Precautions:
Avoid repeated courses and prolonged use; reduce dose in hepatic impairment and renal failure; blood counts required before and during treatment; monitor plasma concentrations in neonates.

Dosage:
Infections due to susceptible organisms (not susceptible to other antimicrobials), by mouth or by intravenous injection or intravenous infusion.
ADULT and CHILD: 50 mg/kg daily in 4 divided doses; up to 100 mg/kg daily in divided doses, in severe infections such as meningitis, septicaemia, and haemophilus epiglottitis (reduce high doses as soon as clinically indicated).
INFANTS under 2 weeks: 25 mg/kg daily in 4 divided doses, 2 weeks to 1 year, 50 mg/kg daily in 4 divided doses.
Epidemics of meningococcal meningitis, by intramuscular injection (of oily injection).
ADULT: 0.5 to 1 g daily; CHILD: 25 mg/kg daily.

Reconstitution and administration
Follow manufacturer's directions. The oily injection is for intramuscular use only.

NOTE: Plasma concentration monitoring required in neonates and preferred in those under 4 years of age; recommended peak plasma concentration (measured approximately 1 hour after intravenous injection or infusion) 15 to 25 mg/litre; pre-dose trough concentration should not exceed 15 mg/litre.

Adverse Effects:
Bone marrow depression, reversible and irreversible aplastic anaemia (with reports of leukaemia), anaemia, leukopenia and thrombocytopenia; nocturnal haemoglobinuria; peripheral neuritis and optic neuritis; nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomatitis, glossitis; hypersensitivity reactions including, rashes, fever, angioedema and rarely anaphylaxis; grey syndrome (vomiting, greenish diarrhoea, abdominal distension, hypothermia, pallid cyanosis, irregular respiration, circulatory collapse) may follow excessive doses in neonates with immature hepatic metabolism; also reported in infants born to mothers treated in late pregnancy.

Porphyria; absence seizures.

Technical Specifications:
Each film coated tablet contains Primaquine phosphate 8.8mg, equivalent to 5mg Primaquine base.

Tablets should be scored with at least one break line to allow for division into equal parts, each containing the proportionate amount of active ingredients.
The salt used and the % of Primaquine base in the salt must be specified on the label and pack insert.
It must be specified whether the dosage strength displayed is that of the salt or the base.

Therapeutic class
Primaquine is a synthetic 8-Aminoquinolone derivative

Standard shelf life
5 years (60 months)

Guidelines for use
For more details, please see
World Health Organisation (WHO), Guidelines for the treatment of Malaria: (www.who.int/malaria/en/)
WHO, Model Lists of Essential Medicines for adults and/or children respectively: (www.who.int/medicines/publications/essentialmedicines/en/index.html)
WHO Model Formulary: (apps.who.int/emlib/Default.aspx?Language=EN)
or your regional and/or national guidelines.

Indications
Radical cure of malaria caused by Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale, in combination with a blood schizonticide like Chloroquine for the erythrocytic parasites.
Elimination of gametocytes of Plasmodium falciparum after routine therapy with a blood schizonticide like Chloroquine.
By mouth (oral)

Storage
Store at temperatures not exceeding 25°C (77°F). Excursions permitted to 15-30°C (59-86°F).
Store in original packaging
Keep out of the reach and sight of children
Protect from light and moisture

Dispensing instructions
To be taken after meals.
Repeat dose if vomiting occurs within one hour of taking the last dose.

General Description:
Quinine-resorcine dihydrochloride sterile solution for I.V/I.M injection, 100mg/ml in 2ml ampoule, containing 61.7% quinine anydrous base, box of 100

Technical Specifications:
Quinine-resorcine dihydrochloride compound sterile solution for I.V/I.M injection, 100mg/ml in 2ml ampoule contains 61.7% quinine anydrous base.

Composition per 100mg
Quinine resorcine dihyrochloride 96.10mg
Quinidine resorcine dihyrochloride 2.55mg
Cinchonine resorcine dihyrochloride 0.68mg
Cinchonidine resorcine dihydrochloride 0.67mg

Note: The most common salt for quinine injection is Quinine dihydrochloride. Quinine bisulfate salts contain only 59.2% Quinine base and are generally not recommended.

The salt used and the % of Quinine base in the salt must be specified on the label and pack insert. It must be specified whether the dosage strength displayed is that of the salt of the base. The method of sterilization must be mentioned in the pack insert.

Therapeutic class:
Quinine is an alkaloid derived from the Cinchona tree.

Standard shelf life:
5 years (60 months)

Guidelines for use:
For more details, please see the links listed below:

WHO Guidelines for the treatment of Malaria


WHO Model Lists of Essential medicines for adults and/or children


WHO Model Formulary


or consult your regional/national guidelines

Indications:
Treatment of multiple drug resistant malaria, often as second line treatment.
Treatment of severe malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum.
Can be considered as alternative therapy for chloroquine sensitive strains of P falciparum, P. ovale, P. malariae and P. vivax.

Route of administration:
By slow intravenous infusion
By intramuscular injection (I.M)
NOT to be given by intravenous injection

Storage:
Store at temperatures not exceeding 25°C (77°F), in original packaging
Do not freeze.
Keep out of the reach and sight of children
Protect from light

Dispensing instructions:
Intravenous infusion
Quinine dihydrochloride injection should be given by a rate controlled infusion in dextrose or physiological saline solutions at a rate not exceeding 5mk salt/kg bw/hr. Must not be given by I.V injection.
Intramuscular injection
Undiluted Quinine dihydrochloride at a concentration of 125mgmg/ml is acidic (pH 2) and painful when given I.M., so it is best diluted to concentrations of 60-100mg/ml.
Quinine dihydrochloride should be given I.M to the anterior thigh, not the buttock, to avoid sciatic nerve injury.
The first dose should be split equally (10mg salt/kg bw) to each thigh.

Electricity generating set, diesel engine driven, trailer mounted with canopy, capable of delivering up to 20 kVA.

**HAZARDOUS MATERIAL - TRANSPORT CERTIFICATE REQUIRED**

Technical Specifications:GENERAL:
A complete diesel generator set including the diesel engine, alternator, control panel, starting equipment, fuel tank and all other accessories for autonomous operation.
RATED POWER:
20 kVA, 16 kW, Power factor (Cos. phi = 0.8), 400/230 V, 3-phase, 50 Hz at NTP (Normal Temperature and Pressure).
ENGINE:
Heavy duty diesel engine, with the following characteristics:
Air cooled.
Synchronous speed: up to 1500 rpm.
Mechanical speed governor.
Heavy duty air cartridge filter.
Cartridge oil filter.
External fuel filter.
Residential silencer.
Electric starter including batteries, leads and automatic battery charging equipment.
FUEL TANK:
Fuel tank of suitable construction with capacity sufficient to run the generator set continuously for 8 hours at the rated capacity.
The tank is provided with suitable piping for connecting it to the engine as well as for filling the tank.
Fuel level indicator placed conveniently on the panel board.
ALTERNATOR:
Synchronous, air cooled and brushless.
Automatic fast voltage regulator, maintaining the output within 2 % under normal conditions.
Screen protected.
CEE Sockets: one 3 pole and one 5 pole.
PANEL BOARD:
Made of steel sheets of appropriate thickness subjected to anti-oxidizing treatment and covered with epoxy resin with suitable protection factor.

The panel board comprises the following:
Automatic main circuit breaker.
Change over switch with positions for:
'MAINS', 'OFF', 'GENERATOR'.
Key to start and stop the unit.
Emergency stop button.
Set-point for speed/governor control.
Set-point for voltage control.
Meters for: Volts (with selector switch to show phases to zero and phase to phase voltages), amperes (three meters or with selector switch to show current in all three phases), frequency, running hours counter.
Warning system for electrical and mechanical alarms.
PROTECTION:
The generator set should be equipped with automatic shutdown equipment if fatal parameters are exceeded including low oil pressure, high engine temperature and belt failure (if applicable).
MOUNTING:
The engine and the alternator should be connected with a heavy-duty elastic coupling and should be mounted on a common rigid base frame with anti-vibration dampers and lifting eyes flexible for transportation.
Engine, alternator, fuel tank and panel should be one integrated unit mounted on trailer with towing bar.
EARTHING:
The generator is supplied with earthing system comprising low resistance rod(s), terminals, cables etc.
ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS:
The rated power of the generator is based on the following environmental conditions:
Altitude: at 150 m above sea level.
- Average yearly temperature...........30°C
- Average 24 hours temperature.........40°C
- Minimum temperature.................-10°C
- Maximum operating temperature........55°C
- Dust storms are expected.
ACCESSORIES:
The following accessories are supplied with the generator set:
Operation and maintenance manuals and spare parts catalogues in English.
Tools kit including pipe spanners for injector's.
Spare parts including:
4 x injectors
6 x oil filters
3 x fuel filters
5 x air filters
1 x fan belt
1 x voltage regulator

A full set of replacement switches/ sensors for detection of fatal parameters (low oil pressure, high engine temperature, belt failure etc.)
CANOPY:
The generator set is mounted in a sound attenuated and weather protective canopy, to reduce the noise level down to 65 dB(A) at a distance of 7 metres.

Packaging and labelling:
The unit is shipped uncrated.

Accessories/Spare parts/Consumables:

5035010 - Distrib.box,port,elec+cables assorted

Weight/Volume/Dimensions:
- estimated weight: 750 kg
- estimated volume: 2.0 cbm

The generator set is used as an electrical power supply for light loads such as lighting and other ordinary office and household needs.

UN number2794
Danger class8

General Description:
Meningitis vaccine, (MENCEVAX) trivalent A,C and W135, vial of 50 dose.

The vaccine consists of purified bacterial polysaccharides from Neisseria meningitidis (meningococcus) of Serogroup A, C and W135. It is a lyophilized powder for reconstitution with diluent for injection. Each 0.5 ml dose of reconstituted vaccine contains 50 µg of each of the polysaccharides of serogroups A, C and W135. It contains lactose/excipient as a stabilizer in q.s for lyophilization. The sterile diluent for multi-dose presentation contains phenol (preservative).

Administration:
The vaccine is for subcutaneous use only. It should under no circumstances be injected by intravenous route. The lyophilized powder must be reconstituted by adding the entire contents of the supplied container of diluent to the vaccine vial. The lyophilized powder should be completely dissolved in the diluent.
The vaccine should be inspected visually for any foreign particulate matter and/or other colouration prior to administration. If observed, the vaccine must be discarded. The sterile diluent for multi-dose presentation (which contains phenol) may show a slight cloudiness and/or pink coloration.

A sterile needle and sterile syringe must be used for each injection. Once the vaccine has been reconstituted, it should be used the same day (preferably immediately but by no means beyond six (6) hours after reconstitution), and only then if the vial has been kept in the refrigerator (+2°C to +8°C) and protected from sun light. Any opened container remaining at the end of a session should be discarded. The vaccine vial monitor, if present, would have been removed on reconstitution.

Immunization A, C, W135 Schedule:
MENCEVAX gives no protection against meningococcal meningitis caused by meningococci belonging to serogroups other than A, C and W135.

The vaccine is indicated for the active immunization of adults and children over 2 years of age. It is particularly recommended for subjects at risk, for example those living in or visiting areas where the disease is epidemic or highly endemic. It is also recommended for subjects living in closed communities and close contacts of patients with disease caused by meningococci of Serogroups A, C and W135.

Vaccination consists of a single injection administered from the age of 2 years and above. According to literature, the duration of post-vaccine immunity is currently 3 years.

Referring to EPI recommendations, Meningococcal vaccine can be given safely and effectively at the same time as other vaccines BCG, DTP, measles, polio (OPV or IPV), hepatitis B and yellow fever vaccines and vitamin A supplementation, but it should be administered at a different site.

Storage:
Meningococcal vaccine should be stored and transported between +2°C to +8°C in the refrigerator. Diluent (buffered isotonic solution) can be stored at room temperature. It is recommended to protect the reconstituted vaccine from direct sunlight.
Do not exceed the expiry date stated on the label and packaging.

Sales Text:
General Description:
DTP, vaccine, adsorbed, vial of 20 doses

The vaccine contains purified diphtheria and tetanus toxoids and inactivated whooping cough organisms. The toxoids are adsorbed onto aluminum phosphate. Thimerosal or Merthiolate (depending on the manufacturer) is used as a preservative (0.01% w/v or 0.05mg or 0.1mg per dose, depending on the manufacturer). The potency of the vaccine per single human dose is at least 4IU for pertussis, 30IU for diphtheria and for tetanus 60IU (determined in mice) or 40IU (determined in guinea pig).

For information on product specifications, refer to the WHO website on Prequalified Vaccines.

Click here

http://www.who.int/immunization_standards/vaccine_quality/PQ_vaccine_lis t_en/en/index.html


Administration:
The vaccine vial should be shaken to homogenize the suspension. The vaccine should be injected intramuscularly or deep subcutaneously. The anterolateral aspect of the upper thigh is the preferred site of injection. (An injection into a child's buttocks may cause injury to the sciatic nerve and is not recommended.) It must not be injected into the skin as this may give rise to local reaction. One dose is 0.5 ml.
A sterile needle and sterile syringe should be used for each injection.

Once opened, multi-dose vials should be kept between +2°C and +8°C.
Multi-dose vials of DTP from which one or more doses of vaccine have been removed during an immunization session may be used in subsequent immunization sessions for up to a maximum of 4 weeks, provided that all of the following conditions are met (as described in the WHO policy statement: The use of opened multi dose vials in subsequent immunization sessions. WHO/V&B/00.09):

The expiry date has not passed;
The vaccines are stored under appropriate cold chain conditions;
the vaccine vial septum has not been submerged in water;
aseptic technique has been used to withdraw all doses;
the vaccine vial monitor (VVM), if attached, has not reached the discard point.

Immunization Schedule:
In countries where pertussis is of particular danger to young infants, DTP immunization should be started as soon as possible with the first dose given as early as 6 weeks, and two subsequent doses given at 4-week intervals.

DTP vaccine can be given safely and effectively at the same time as BCG, measles and polio vaccines (OPV and IPV), hepatitis B, haemophilus influenzae type b, yellow fever vaccine and vitamin A supplementation.
WHO recommends that, where resources permit, an additional dose of DTP be given approximately one year after completion of the primary doses. However, the need for additional booster doses of DTP, DT or Td should be addressed by individual national immunization programmes.

DTP vaccine can be given safely at the same time as other EPI vaccine according to national immunization schedules.

Transport and Storage:
DTP vaccine should be stored and transported between +2°C and +8°C.
The vaccine must not be frozen.

One dose of 0.5 ml at an elected date.
A second dose of vaccine should be given after an interval of at least three weeks. See section 5.1.

Children and adolescents aged 9-17 years:
One dose of 0.5 ml at an elected date.
Immunogenicity data obtained at three weeks after administration of Focetria in clinical studies suggest that a single dose may be sufficient. If a second dose is administered there should be an interval of at least three weeks between the first and second dose.

Children aged 3-8 years:
One dose of 0.5 ml at an elected date.
Preliminary immunogenicity data obtained in a limited number of children show that there is a further immune response to a second dose of 0.5 ml administered after an interval of three weeks. The use of a second dose should take into consideration the information provided in section 5.1.

Children aged 6 months to 35 months:
One dose of 0.5 ml at an elected date.
A second dose of vaccine should be given after an interval of at least three weeks.

Vaccination is not currently recommended in this age group.

It is recommended that subjects who receive a first dose of Focetria, should complete the vaccination course with Focetria.

Caution is needed when administrating this vaccine to persons with a known hypersensitivity (other than anaphylactic reaction) to the active substance, to any of the excipients, to thiomersal and to residues (eggs and chicken protein, ovalbumin, kanamycin and neomycin sulphate, formaldehyde and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB)).

As with all injectable vaccines, appropriate medical treatment and supervision should always be readily available in case of a rare anaphylactic event following the administration of the vaccine.

If the pandemic situation allows, immunisation should be postponed in patients with severe febrile illness or acute infection.

There are no data with Focetria using the subcutaneous route. Antibody response in patients with endogenous or iatrogenic immunosuppression may be insufficient.

A protective response may not be elicited in all vaccinees.

Common: nausea

STORAGE
Keep out of reach and sight of children.
Store between +2°C and +8°C in the original package in order to protect from light until the expiry date indicated on the vial. DO NOT FREEZE

Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, 7-valent, suspension for injection, prefilled syringe without fixed needle.

Each dose of 0.5 ml contains:
Pneumococcal polysaccharide serotype 4 2 micrograms
Pneumococcal polysaccharide serotype 6B 4 micrograms
Pneumococcal polysaccharide serotype 9V 2 micrograms
Pneumococcal polysaccharide serotype 14 2 micrograms
Pneumococcal polysaccharide serotype 18C 2 micrograms
Pneumococcal polysaccharide serotype 19F 2 micrograms
Pneumococcal polysaccharide serotype 23F 2 micrograms

The serotypes are conjugated to the CRM197 carrier protein and adsorbed on aluminium phosphate (0.5 mg). The vaccine does not contain a preservative. Exipients are sodium chloride and water for injections. Contraindications are hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the excipients, or to diphtheria toxoid.

Indications:
The vaccine is approved for active immunisation against disease caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae
serotypes contained in the vaccine in infants and children from two months up to five years of age. Serious diseases that are often caused by pneumococci include pneumonia, meningitis and febrile bacteraemia; otitis media, sinusitis and bronchitis are more common but less serious manifestations of infection.

Administration:
The vaccine should be given by intramuscular injection. The preferred sites are anterolateral aspect of the thigh (vastus lateralis muscle) in infants or the deltoid muscle of the upper arm in young children.

Immunization Schedule:
Trials in several developing countries have demonstrated the efficacy of a 3-dose schedule for infants without a subsequent booster dose.

A single catch-up dose may be given to previously unvaccinated children aged 12-24 months and to children aged 2-5 years who are at high risk.
In countries where mortality among children aged <5 years is >50/1,000 live births or where >50,000 children die annually it should be considered a priority to include this vaccine in the national immunization programme(1)

The vaccine can be administered simultaneously with other paediatric vaccines in accordance with the recommended immunisation shedules. Different injectable vaccines should always be given at different injection sites.

Pack size of 10 pre-filled syringes.

The vaccine should be stored and transported between +2°C and +8°C.

The flipchart easel should be able to be used both to hang flipchart paper on and to use as a white board.

The centres of these holes are at: 9 cm, 12 cm, 19 cm, 49 cm, 56 cm and 59 cm (as per the attached design).

The legs should be tripod in structure for ease of movement and the legs should be height adjustable, lockable and securely attached to the frame. The height adjustment may be via a telescopic or lever controlled design. The legs should be extendable to allow the height of the easel to extend over a 1 m range. The legs should be easy to extend and retract and the collapsed height should be close to the dimensions of the whiteboard surface for ease of storage.
The design, material and mode of attachment of the legs should ensure stability, even on uneven surfaces. The feet should be covered in a durable material to reduce skidding and to stabilize the easel on surfaces.

The pen tray should ensure that there is enough space for dusters, cloth and extra flipchart markers. The pen tray should be sturdy and securely attached to the whiteboard frame.

The surface of the whiteboard should be smooth, scratch/dent resistant and easy to clean. Markings from whiteboard markers must be completely removable by a dry cloth. The whiteboard frame should have rounded corners with no sharp edges. The whiteboard must be firmly fixed to the frame. The whiteboard may also be magnetic but this is not a requirement. In the event that a magnetic board is presented, then at least 4 in number magnets should be supplied for use and should be strong enough to hold 80 gsm sheets of flipchart paper to the board.

The easel should be sufficiently durable to withstand extended use in a variety of climates (large temperature ranges and humidities) and should be suitable for outdoor use.

General Description:
Lightweight electrical submersible dewatering or desludging pump for heavily contaminated water with solids up to 50 mm in diameter. Maximum head is 20 m.
A suitable PETROL generator is included in the kit.

Technical Specifications:
Pump set
2" submersible / immersible pump with cast iron casing, screw type impeller and tandem mechanical seals running in oil bath. Directly driven by 1.5 kW, 400 V, 3 phase, 50 Hz, IP68 motor. The pump is free-standing on its feet. Complete with male hose tail outlet and 25 meters of cable with 16 A plug fed from the generator set. The lead will be looped and cleated around the pump handle to prevent pulling on the internal connections.
A removable anti-dive plate will be attached to the pump to prevent 'boring' in muddy conditions.

Generator
6000 Watt 400 Volt 3 phase 50 cycles brushless generator fitted with hours counter, 1 x 16 Amp output socket protected by a power circuit breaker (ground fault detector) earth leakage trip to prevent fatal electric shocks should the power lead or pump develop a fault or be damaged. The generator shall be flanged coupled to the driving petrol engine.

Engine
OHV petrol engine governed to run at 3000 rpm complete with recoil start, 3 hour fuel tank, low oil protection exhaust system, air and oil filters.

The generator and the engine shall be mounted on anti-vibration mounts inside a robust roll frame.

The Pump and Genset are supplied with following Accessories/Spareparts/Consumables:

Accessories
40 m Pump supporting rope (16 mm)
20 m Electrical extension cable with socket connectors
20 m Cable protection hose (fitted)
25 m 2" lay-flat canvas delivery hose & 2" hose clip
1 x Sliding collar to fit over the lay-flat where it exits the well
1 x 2" BSPT male coupling
1 x Two-wheel site trolley for generator set
1 x Tool kit comprising spark plug spanner, screw driver and oil drain spanner
5 x 1.4 litre containers of engine oil (allowing four complete refills plus spillage)
1 x Operators Manual

Spares
One set of spares for 1000 hours operation comprising:
2 x Spark plugs
2 x Air filter elements
1 x 16 A plug
1 x 2" hose clip

Transport and storage:
Packaging: All the items shall be packed in a sturdy plywood case suitable for sea freight clearly marked with "S5006016_Electrical Dewatering Pump with Genset, PETROL", the gross weight and dimensions. Marks shall be on the front and back of the case, as determined by the runners of the forklift.

Instruction for use:
Use in:
Dewatering
Desludging
Combating localised flooding
Cleaning wells
The maximum head of the pump is 20 m; this package is designed to dewater wells at around a depth of 15 m. If higher heads are required, then two pumps of this type can be coupled together to give a maximum head of 40 m (7 m3/ hr at 35 m head) (see below instructions).
This pump does not pump air; it does not need to be submersed to pump as in the second pump when pumping in series, but when switching on there should always be water in the pump chamber or the seals will burn in 1 - 2 minutes.
The purpose of the base plate is to prevent the legs of the pump sinking in to the mud causing the impeller to try and drill itself downwards, which results in the pump becoming clogged up. If the base plate is not present either suspend the pump just above the muddy bottom, turn it on its side or put it in a large perforated bucket.
If the pump is near its maximum pumping depth the canvas lay-flat may need to be attached to a stake at the top of the well to prevent sliding back into the well. A hose connector can be attached to the end of the lay-flat to make it easier to tie to a stake.
This pump can be used for desludging latrine pits.

Instructions for coupling two pumps together in series:
Using the rope provided, the lower pump shall be suspended (by a loop around the handle) at the bottom of the well. The second pump should be suspended some 15 m above the first pump. If two pumps are being used suspend each pump with a separate rope. Great care should be taken when lowering the pumps and gloves should be worn.
Remove the base plate of the second pump and connect the lay-flat distribution hose from the first pump into the bottom of the second pump, the kit contains a male connector for this purpose.
The electrical extension lead should be attached to the cable form the first pump. The connector is splash proof but not water proof, so avoid submerging this connection under water.

Regularly maintain the engine according to the manual (On the SD Intranet a sample template is posted to assist with the maintenance of the engine). See the generator maintenance sheet via the following link:
http://danaapps01.unicef.org/Denmark/DO/daniclguide.nsf/Pg/h0103

Trained staff required for O&M
Choice of petrol or diesel generator determined by availability on-ground and ease of supply.

This is similar to Oxfam kit (code WSDP/6)

Used for resolution of localised (stationary) flooding and dewatering of hand-dug wells

Determined by context and application

Not to be used in fast flowing water where anchoring in preferred vertical position is difficult

Other Emergency scenario considerations:
In general high volume low lift application
Not designed for continuous use

General Description:
Water purification unit, skid mounted with a capacity of 5 cubic meters per hour at 20 m (TMH) Total Manometric Head. Diesel operated generator.

Technical Specifications:
The unit is designed to purify 5 cubic meters per hour at 20 meters TMH of surface water from rivers, lakes or shallow wells having maximum turbidity of 20 (N.T.U.) Nephelometric Turbidity Units.
The unit is capable of producing drinking water free of the physical and bacteriological contaminations according to the WHO recommendations for drinking water.
The unit will not take care of industrial contamination, such as hydrocarbons, chemical waste, etc.
All material used in the unit that are in contact with water must be certified and approved for use with drinking water.

As standard, the unit is skid mounted, but can also be supplied as trailer mount (see below Optional Supplies (c)); the system also does NOT contain: Water Storage and Distribution kit (Collapsible water storage tanks, connection hose kit and tap stand kit). This Distribution kit can, if required, be ordered and supplied together with the Purification Unit (see below Optional Supplies (b)).

The following steps are followed in the water treatment process:

1. Surface water intake: Floating raw water suction by means of an electrical submersible pump or by a diesel driven motor pump with adequate suction hose, inlet strainer of less than 2 mm openings, and a feed hose up to the treatment unit.

2. Pre-chlorination by Calcium Hypochlorite; this includes the container and equipment for the preparation of the solution and/or dosing of the predetermined amount of Chlorine.

3. Coagulation by Aluminum Sulphate; this includes the container and equipment for the preparation of the solution and/or dosing of the predetermined amount of Aluminum Sulphate

4. Flocculation; a flocculation unit allowing sufficient contact time for adequate creation of floc for sedimentation or filtration.
NOTE: Sedimentation; this compartment is not included in this basic treatment unit for air shipment. To be ordered separately, if desired(see below Optional Supplies (a)).

5. Filtration; this includes a sand filter and an activated carbon filter. The filters are complete with all the back wash piping, valves, manometers and controls.

6. Disinfection; by Chlorination. A dose of residual Chlorine is added to guard against subsequent contamination during storage. For chemical shipping reasons NaDCC is shipped instead of Calcium Hypochlorite HTH. However, once on-site, the dosing equipment can be employed with other chlorination products such as HTH and Sodium Hypochlorite. (see also below option for Solar powered Chlorine Generator for on-site production of Sodium Hypochlorite solution - option (d))

Sedimentation: if sedimentation/settlement of floc must be processed, an ADDITIONAL water reservoir (settlement compartment) should be ordered separately. It is preferably an option with the purification unit S0005846 for Sea Shipment.
A contact time for about one hour should be allowed for the chemicals to react and the solids to settle. The sedimentation chamber should have all the facilities for the periodic removal of the sediments as well as passing the clarified water to the next stage of treatment.

Power System: The purification unit is of autonomous operation. This is provided by means of one (or two) diesel driven motor pump(s) supplied with the unit.

The system is supplied with:
Suction hose
Consumables for minimum three (up to six) months of operation.
A set of spare parts needed for all the parts including the pump, sufficient for 2000 hours of normal operation.
A set of tools for the operator as needed for the normal operation and maintenance.
A simple visual water testing kit.
Operating manuals in (English, French, Spanish and Arabic).

Optionally the System can be supplied with:
a) Sedimentation Kit: For sedimentation/settlement of floc to be processed, supplied as an intermediate water reservoir (or as special settlement compartment) with necessary accessories.
A contact time for about one hour should be allowed for the chemicals to react and the solids to settle. The sedimentation chamber should have all the facilities for the periodic removal of the sediments as well as passing the clarified water to the next stage of treatment - Order w/catalogue product number S0005872.

b) Water Storage kit composed of a double set of (2) collapsible water storage tanks (Water Bladders) of each 10 000 litres capacity (of a quality similar to UNICEF catalogue product number S0005834) with 20 meters hose (of a quality similar to UNICEF catalogue product number 0008029) for connecting the unit to the tank with the required quick coupling.
- For Water Storage kit (without Tap Stands) - Order w/catalogue product number S0005873.
- For Water Distribution Tap Stand kit (1x6 taps) - Order w/catalogue product number S0005831

c) One-axle trailer mounting with storage room(s) for the Purification unit pump, hoses and accessories - Order w/catalogue product number S0005874.

d) Chlorine Generator (Electro-Chlorinator) kit for on-site production of Sodium Hypochlorite solution by electrolysis of salt water (brine) - in replacement of HTH or NaDCC purchase. This Chlorine Generator is Solar powered in order to be used with the non-electric water purification units. The kit contains the electrode with adequate solar panel and accessories.
For Chlorine Generator - Order w/catalogue product number S0005876.

Transport and Storage:
The unit is packed in wooden boxes on the skid or the trailer as the option selected.
Store in a dry and well ventilated room

The unit is used for providing drinking water for about 5,000 residents or displaced population in cases of emergency where the source is surface water having not more than 20 NTU. In the water treatment process, these steps have to be followed:

1. Raw water suction and straining; by submersible pump or by motor pump complete with the suction hose, and inlet strainer of approximately 2 mm openings.

2. Pre-chlorination by Calcium Hypochlorite or NaDCC.

3. Coagulation/flocculation by Aluminum Sulphate.

4. Sedimentation is optional; sedimentation chamber must be ordered clearly with the order if required. It has all the facilities for the periodic removal of the sediments as well as passing the clarified water to the next stage of treatment. It can also be added to the system later. --NOTE: this Sedimentation Compartment is not included in the basic treatment unit. To be ordered specifically, if desired (see below Optional Supplies (a)).

5. Filtration; by a sand filter and an activated carbon filter.

6. Back washing; a back washing system is integrated in the system.

7. Disinfection; by Chlorination. a dose of residual Chlorine is added to guard against subsequent contamination during storage.

General Description:
Compression sprayer, Hand operated, for chlorine/pesticide and insecticide applications, 7.4 Liters.

Technical specifications:
Hand operated compression sprayer for chlorine/pesticide and insecticide applications (HCS), with a capacity of 7.4 liters.
The sprayer shall include the following:
Tank, cylindrical shape,
equipped with a hand operated air pump
with two handed handle
and locking device separate from the tank lid,
pressure release safety device,
Pressure relief (safety) valve device,
air pressure gauge,
Shut-off valve to keep the pressure in the tank if the hose and the discharge set removed,
hose attached at the top of the tank to a dip tube,
trigger valve with locking off device,
lance,
control flow valve
and nozzle.

The sprayer shall be equipped with a system for hanging the lance when the sprayer is not in use.
The operation pressure of the sprayer shall be 4 bar (unless otherwise specified).
Construction materials of the sprayer shall be free from tin, lead and wood and materials shall be corrosion, pressure and UV resistant. They shall be in conformity with specifications of the WHO 2010 revised edition of Vector Control Equipment.
The maximum total weight of the sprayer shall not exceed 25 KG when the sprayer is filled with liquid according to the manufacturer maximum recommended capacity.
The tank opening filler shall be equipped with a filter and its dimensions shall be not less than 90 mm in minor axis.

SPRAYER TANK:
The tank shall be made from robust and chemical resistance material, with operation capacity of 7.4 Litres (approximately).
The sprayer shall be clearly and permanently marked with a horizontal permanent line to indicate the maximum liquid volume in litres. Other marking should indicate 1-litre graduation.

Pressure relief (safety) valve device:
A pressure relief valve shall be provided with the sprayer to prevent the pressurization in the tank beyond the limits prescribed by the manufacturer ± 10 % for safety. The valve shall re-seal after activation, allowing the normal operation of the sprayer without any leakage.

Markings:
The sprayer shall be clearly and permanently marked with a horizontal permanent line indicating the maximum liquid volume in litres. Other marking should indicate 1-litre graduation.

AIR PUMP:
The tank, filled with liquid to the maximum operational capacity, shall reach the operational pressure on completion of no more than 60 full strokes of the pump. At the maximum recommended operational pressure/capacity; pump’s check valves shall prevent any leakage of the liquid into the pump’s cylinder.

Handle and plunger rod:
The handle shall be T handle and shall be made from galvanized tubular steel or better and coated with high quality epoxy. The handle shall be designed in a way that the sprayer can be easily carried by this handle when it’s filled to the maximum recommended capacity. The plunger rod shall be made from galvanized steel or better. Pump’s cylinder shall be made from brass.

DISCHARGE SYSTEM:
Filters:
The sprayer shall be equipped with two filters; one at the trigger valves and one in the nozzle. The filter in the trigger valve must be smaller than the size of the nozzle aperture and not larger than 50 mesh size. Filters shall be manufactured with a proper size to prevent passage of particles that would cause nozzle blockage. Filters shall be made from pesticide/insecticide formulations resistant materials and shall be cleanable/replaceable.

Hose:
The hose shall be of high pressure hose type lined with chemical-oil resistance liner. The hose shall be suitable for pesticide and insecticide products, including chlorine. Hose’s length shall be 1.5 m or longer.

Trigger valve:
The trigger valve must have a positive lock-off position. Valve’s lever length shall be 100 mm or longer, measured from the pivot point. The valve's lever shall be easily moved by the operator hand. Trigger valve shall be made from brass. Sprayer shall be drip-less sprayer.

Lance:
The lance shall be made from brass and its length shall be 50 cm or longer.
Flow rate control device:
The sprayer shall be equipped with flow rate control device to maintain a relatively even discharge rate and a uniform nozzle pressure. Bidder/manufacturer shall mention the flow rate/type of this flow regulator valve. Tolerance limits of the specified flow rate shall be ± 5 % of the manufacturer specified flow. Test method will be according to paragraph 2.10.4 in WHO 2010 revised edition of vector control equipment.

Nozzle/Nozzle tip:
Bidder/Supplier shall declare the availability of following nozzle types: Nozzle types are solid or jet stream nozzle, flat spray nozzle deliver fan-shaped spray, hollow cone nozzle, and solid cone nozzle; nozzle type shall be specified by the country office. The type of the nozzle tip and the flow rate shall be stated by the bidder/manufacturer and they shall comply with the corresponding international standards. Tolerance limits of the discharge rate shall not exceed ± 5 % when tested in accordance to section 2.10.5.1 in WHO 2010 revised edition of vector control equipment. Nozzle and Nozzle tip shall be made from hardened stainless steel or ceramic.

Sprayer’s seal ring:
All seal ring shall be made from Viton or better.

SPRAYER CARRYING SYSTEM:
The carrying system shall be shoulder carrying system. Bidders are encouraged to provide a design with a back carrying system with a suitable spacer to prevent the contact between the person and the sprayer’s tank.

Straps and fastening:
Straps width shall be at least 50 mm with a tolerance of 5 mm. Straps shall be adjustable for at least 100 cm in length. The straps, fastenings and strap clips shall not show structural failure when subject to the strap drop test according to section 2.12 in WHO 2010 revised edition of vector control equipment. Straps shall not increase in weight by more than 10 % when they subjected to the absorbency test according to section 2.12 in WHO 2010 revised edition of vector control equipment.

The sprayer shall be supplied with:
Equipment description and detailed technical data sheet.
Operating instruction.
Maintenance instruction.
A list of spare parts

Certification/Tests:
Sprayer, sprayer’s parts and accessories shall be certified to and might be required subject to pass the tests stated in section two (2) in Equipment for Vector Control Specification Guidelines, WHO revised edition 2010.

Bidders are required to provide documentary evidence of compliance of quoted product(s) with WHO guidelines for hand-operated compression sprayers: quality control certificate from WHO collaborating centre or similar.
The offer shall be accompanied with relevant sprayer technical data sheets.
Any potential deviation to the specifications as well as further relevant clarifications to the offer shall be clearly indicated with the offer.

Short Description
Chlorine and pH Test Strips - 2 in 1 indicator, for visual comparison.

Technical Specifications:
Low range Chlorine 2-in-1 Rapid Test Strips for simultaneous testing of both Free Chlorine and pH in Drinking Water. Simple Dip-and-Read procedure for results in seconds.

For testing of Free Chlorine (0-10ppm) and pH (6.0-9.0) in the water with the following scales:

Free Chlorine: 0.0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 3.0, 6.0, 10.0ppm
pH: 6.0, 6.4, 6.8, 7.2, 7.6, 7.8, 8.2, 9.0

This test strip technology is TMB (Tetramethyl Benzidine) based. It shows equivalent results to DPD comparison technologies (Around 99% certified correlation with DPD), being drinking water compliant. The range of the free chlorine test pad allows both low and high levels of chlorine to be monitored.
The indicator for pH is Bromothymol Blue pH, having easy to read blue colours.
All of the reagents are impregnated on the test strip pad, and no external chemicals are needed to perform the water quality test. The test strip is resistant to interference from Monochloramines. Results are comparable to technologies using soluble DPD1 & pH tablets/powders with simple visual block, pool or disc Comparator.
The test strip is USEPA approved for drinking water compliance.

It is a simple, easy to use test strip for visually testing chlorine and pH of the water, with a simple Dip and Read procedure yielding rapid results (approximately 30 seconds).

Test procedure: Dip one strip in the water for 10 seconds with a gentle back and forth motion. Remove the strip, shake once, briskly, to remove excess water and wait about 10 seconds. Then match pH and free chlorine results with the supplied colour chart.

The Kit includes 100 test strips contained in a water and humidity tight bottle/container, including instructions for use and storage.
It is supplied with an appropriate easy to read Colour Comparison Chart, and as appropriate with Temperature Compensation Chart.

Shelf life: 24 Months (storage temperature not exceeding 32 oC)
After unsealing of the cap, the non-used test strips stored in the re-closed container/bottle are expected to maintain their capacity within the shelf life indication.

General Description:
Add-On kit for use with standard squatting plate of dimensions 120 cm x 80 cm. This kit is designed to enhance accessibility and use of a squatting plate by children and adults with disabilities.

Technical specifications:
Add-On kit for use with standard squatting plate of dimensions 120 cm x 80 cm (UNICEF Catalogue Material code S5007335). This kit is designed for children and adults with disabilities, particularly those with mobility difficulties, to facilitate use when installed on one squatting plate.

Each kit is easy to assemble to provide a stable and durable installation for one latrine in emergencies. Used with family or communal latrine slabs, or in health centres, feeding centres, temporary learning centres and schools, child friendly spaces, etc., it is composed of an elevated toilet seat with a support frame capable of supporting the weight of a person during the independent or assisted transfer of people with disabilities to and from the seat (for example transferring from a wheelchair). The superstructure of selected latrines should be wide enough to allow a person with a wheelchair to enter and maneuver.

The kit is complete, ready to install by non-technicians, and does not require any materials to be sourced in country for the initial installation. (However, potential repairs can be made with locally available materials).

This Add-On kit is foreseen for deployment with a ratio of 1:10 slab among a multiple squatting plates installation1. The latrine slabs and Add-on kits are supplied separately.

Add-on structure and seat technical details:

The kit is composed of a sturdy handrail and support structure, together with an elevated seat.

The structures and their coatings are of lightweight, rigid, durable and sturdy design, climatically stable and is resistant to heat, water and especially to manual cleaning with/without cleaning agents.

The structure is designed to be sufficiently strong, sturdy and at the appropriate height to allow comfortable support for an adult person with a disability, rails are at an appropriate height and distance to support children and smaller adolescents with or without disabilities to access the seat with ease. The rails can also be used by people who are blind and visually impaired to guide them to the seat. The elevated seat is designed to ensure that there is suitable comfort and support when seating. The seat comes with a feature (cover, self-closing silicone tube, or equivalent) to avoid smell and flies to circulate to and from the pit.

The joining of the seat to the squatting slab is also designed to reduce smells and insects from the pit escaping into the cubicle. Consideration for hygiene and cleaning has also been given to the joints between the steel support and the latrine slab, i.e. for ease of slab cleaning and to avoid dirt accumulation in these joints. Any product employed as sealing of joints has a smooth and non-sticky finishing.

The structure has a maximum weight of 15kg, which reduces the maximum load-bearing capacity of the plastic slabs at their centre (requested to be minimum 150kg by design at the centre).

The add-on kit is supplied with clear assembling and installation manual/instructions, and all tools are included.

The latrine add-on kit currently comes in 2 distinct models with their specificities and compatibility constraints. The current price range of the models is USD 90 – 265. The recommended add-on model will depend on the existing or procured plastic slabs brand/model, therefore information on those plastic slabs must be communicated by CO to SD prior to/when ordering, in order to ensure maximum compatibility.


The ratio of 1:10 is an overall guide for procurement. The proportion in each site will depend on the context, for example where there are multiple latrines in the same location, 10% should be accessible. While in a health post with only one latrine, this should be accessible.

Packing:
The kit shall be flat packed/stacked the most compact possible to allow for easy and cost-effective transport and storage.

General Description:
Add-On kit for use with standard squatting plate of dimensions 120 cm x 80 cm. This kit is designed for children and disabled people to facilitate the use when installed on one squatting plate.

Technical specifications:
Add-On kit for use with standard squatting plate of dimensions 120 cm x 80 cm (UNICEF Catalogue Material code S5007335). This kit is designed for children and disabled people to facilitate the use when installed on one squatting plate.

The kit is easy to assemble to provide a stable and durable installation for one latrine in emergencies. Used with family or communal latrine slabs, or in health centres, feeding centres, schools etc., it is composed of an elevated toilet seat with support frame rails capable of supporting the weight of a person during potential autonomous physical displacement of disabled people.

The kit shall be complete, ready to install, and not requiring any materials to be sourced in country for the initial installation. (However, it is allowed to foresee the design for later repairs with locally available materials).

This Add-On kit is foreseen for deployment with a limited number of single slabs in a multiple squatting plates installation. The latrine slabs and Add-on kits are supplied separately.

The Add-On kit with seat and handle rail structure is designed to fit as minimum one model type of the different squatting slabs supplied through UNICEF SD, and ideally versatile enough to fit several different squatting slab designs, potentially as a standardized kit or as an adaptable kit able to fit more than one squatting slab design. This under consideration of the manufacturer related slightly different drop hole and foot step designs and their interrelated measures of the different squatting plate manufactures on the market.

ADD-ON STRUCTURE AND SEAT

The kit is basically composed of a sturdy hand rail and support structure, together with an elevated seat.

The structures and their potential coatings shall be of lightweight, rigid, durable and sturdy design, climatically stable and resistant to heat, water and not least to manual cleaning with/without cleaning agents.

The structure is designed sufficiently strong, sturdy and high enough to allow a comfortable support for an adult person with physical disabilities, while rails are not too distant to allow supporting also children and smaller youngsters with or without disabilities to access the seat with ease.
The elevated seat design will help to ensure that there is suitable comfort and support when seating.

The hand rail and support structure is composed of steel tubes that, once assembled and firmly fixed to the squatting slab, will be strong and stable enough to securely allow one adult person lifting the person’s own weight in the arms for displacement on the slab into and away from the toilet seat. The hand rail support can potentially be equipped with an intermediate rest seat or other tubular design to assist the person’s displacement.

The seat module is either an individual seat fixed directly into the drop hole area by the bottom of the module, or a seat integrated and supported by the tubular steel support frame.
The seat module has a bowl extension until the drop hole to avoid splashing outside the drop hole area. The downwards tube extension is large enough to diminish dirt accumulation and slim enough to avoid toddlers to accidentally pass through.

The seat arrangement has a cover system to avoid smell and flies etc. This cover system can either be a direct on seat lid (traditional toilet flip-down lid type), or alternatively a bottom cover which can have different designs such as a silicone self-closing tube, a counter-weight self-closing horizontal door/trap, or a water-seal based P- or S-trap, under consideration of appropriateness and water availability at the installation site.

The hand rail frame and the toilet seat have firm hold-down attachments (bolts or similar click-on for the seat/sliding arrangements/bolting for the frame) to fix them sturdily to the borders and drop hole of the standard 120 x 80 cm latrine slab.

The jointing arrangements between the seat module and the squatting slab must be designed to avoid as much as possible smells and insects from the latrine pit. It can be necessary to include butyl sealants or similar with the kit to ensure appropriately closed joints. The same can be necessary for hygienic reasons with the joints between the steel support and the latrine slab, i.e. for ease of slab cleaning and to avoid dirt accumulation in these joints. Any product employed as sealing of joints shall have a smooth and non-sticky finition.

The Add-On Kit is supplied with clear assembling and installation manual/instructions, and as appropriate including clear instructions for application of potential sealing materials.

PACKING
The kit shall be flat packed/stacked the most compact possible to allow for easy and cost effective transport.

Accommodation unit with washroom for 2 persons with standard furniture and accessories as per floor plan drawings - Accommodation Unit 1/A & 1/B

Module 6000x3000 on subfloor (surface area of the modular structure measures approximately 18 m2).
The entire framing structure is comprised of cold-formed galvanized sheet sections and belts of e=1.5 mm. All necessary joints for forming the framing are made by welding and/or special bolting.
The exterior enclosure is made of 60mm-thick sandwich panel comprised of pre-lacquered steel plant on galvanized base on both sides and heat insulation and soundproofing in between, comprised of gunned polyurethane resins with a density of 40 kg/m3 (± 10%) and a heat conductivity factor of λ=0,021 W/mK. The panels is secured to the framing by means of concealed bolts. Façade finished in lacquered folded sheeting. The panel is high moisture-resistant.
Interior partition thickness: 40mm
The roof is comprised of AIS-5G paneling, with a thickness of 80mm. The roof panel is of the same characteristics as the side enclosure panel as far as densities and composition are concerned. The eave runs around the entire perimeter of the unit, the fronts and sides being finished in lacquered galvanized steel of the same color as the roof panel. The panels are secured to the framing by means of special bolting. Polyurethane-based elastomer putties are used for sealing joints and seams.
Exterior Finish Color: White – Interior Finish: GN Pyrenees White.
Comprised of 1.5 m. cold-formed longitudinal and cross galvanized steel sections. Plywood boarding, e_18 mm, is placed over these sections and then covered in MOD. TRAVIATA 6026 SINTASOL brand floor covering. The subfloor is insulated by means of AIS-PRT paneling 40 mm in thickness.
Feet adjustable in height.
The windows are two-leaf sliding windows in white PVC, dimensions 975x1200 with 4/6/4 glass, blind and insect screen.
The doors are made of white lacquered aluminium and panel leaf with both sided in white lacquered galvanized sheeting with polyurethane insulation. Doors are equipped with blind-panel leaves, handles and lock. Dimensions: 975x2060.

Modular Design
Possibility of expansion according to needs, expandable by connecting with other units

Hydraulic System
The bathroom fixtures are white porcelains of the Roca brand or similar. The plumbing facility is comprised of multilayer polyethylene waffle pipe with their fittings. The sewerage is comprised of rigid PVC pipe and accessories, equipped with the respective hydraulic syphons. The seams will be made by means of specific PVC adhesives in order to achieve a perfectly watertight seal complete with (as per floor plan drawings - Accommodation Unit 1/A & 1/B).

·Complete porcelain toilet with low tank
·Porcelain sink with complete pedestal equipped with hot/cold faucet.
·Shower plate. Dimensions: 800x800 mm with hot/cold faucet
·Electric hot water heater, 50-liter capacity.

Electrical System
All of the electrical lines and their facilities adhere to the current European standards and low-voltage regulations. At the service connection entry point, a Control and Fuse Panel is installed for independent protection by means of circuit breakers and differentials necessary for lighting, climatizing and sundry uses, and will be fitted with elements safeguarding against direct contact, power surges and short-circuits and indirect contact.
The electrical facility is comprised of (as per floor plan drawings - Accommodation Unit 1/A & 1/B).

·Point of light
·Wall sockets 16A+TT (watertight seal in bathrooms).
·Switches and/or Toggles 10A+TT.
·Wall-mounted exhaust-fan
·Smoke detector

General Description:
Chlorine, NaDCC 56%, for Water purification, as Sodium Dichloroisocyanurate (NaDCC) granules, in plastic pot of 0.5kg. Supplied with measuring spoon.

Technical specifications:
Chlorine as 100% Sodium Dichloroisocyanurate Dihydrate (NaDCC) in white granules, which releases 56% of available Chlorine:
Suitable for treatment of water for human consumption (drinking water purification).
Shelf life (expected): 3 years (Unopened container)

Supplied with measuring spoon, short handle,
Volume 20 ml (= 15 g of granules),

Including instructions leaflet

The Sodium Dichloroisocyanurate Dihydrate (NaDCC) compound must be certified by NSF International (or delegated organism) to the NSF/ANSI standard 60. The product must also comply with the EN 12931:2015 standard.

USER AND STORAGE PRECAUTION NOTE:
This NaDCC product should not be mixed with incompatible materials such as organic materials, nitrogen containing materials, other oxidizers, acids, bases, oils, grease, sawdust, and dry fire-extinguishers containing monoammonium compounds. In particular, the NaDCC should not be mixed with Calcium Hypochlorite (HTH).
Though the pots give good protection if kept closed, it is strongly recommended, if practical, to store them apart from incompatible materials.

Packaging and labeling:
As per Hazardous Goods notes:
Bulk granules in container (appropriate plastic pot) of 0.5 kg NaDCC total.
This pack size is normally allowed for all transport modes, including passenger flights.

Storage and transportation:
Storage: Keep in a cool dry place, out of direct sunlight.
Store in original container where temperatures do not exceed 50 degrees Celsius.
The container must be re-sealed immediately after opening to minimize any moisture intake.
Keep out of the reach of children.

Conserver le récipient a l'abri de la chaleur et de l'humidité, ne pas dépasser 50 dégrées Celsius.
Refermer le récipient immédiatement après ouverture pour minimiser l’entré d’humidité.
Tenir hors de la portée des enfants.

Hazardous Goods notes:
As the product container totalise a maximum content of 0.5kg it is not classified as dangerous goods for transport:

ADR SP 375: Packaging of 5 kg or less are not subject to any provisions of this Code, provided packaging meets the general provisions

IMDG 2014 (2.10.2.7): Packaging of 5 kg or less are not subject to any provisions of this Code, provided packaging meets the general provisions of 4.1.1.1, 4.1.1.2, 4.1.1.4 and 4.1.1.8.

IMO/ICAO/IATA: UN No.3077, Class 9, Packing group III

Directions for use and dosage:
1/- To obtain a 0.5 percent Chlorine solution: Pour 1 spoon of NaDCC Granules in 1.5 litre of water. Stir to dissolve. Appr. 10 spoons for one Oxfam type bucket of 14 liters.
The 0.5% (= 5,000mg/l available chlorine) solution is used directly for SURFACE disinfection.

2/- To obtain a 1 percent Chlorine solution: Weigh out and dissolve 20g of NaDCC Granules in 1 litre of water. Stir to dissolve.
The 1% (= 10,000mg/l available chlorine) solution is used to disinfect larger quantities of WATER, as following examples:
- For 1 mg/l in 10 Litres water, add 1 ml solution
-For 5 mg/l in 10 Litres water, add 5 ml solution
NOTE: 1mg/l = 1 ppm available chlorine.

DRINKING WATER:
1/- Pre-treatment/simple filtering can be necessary to ensure that the water turbidity is less than 5 NTU before chlorinating.
2/- Ensure that a minimum contact time of 30 minutes is allowed before consumption.
3/- Ensure a thorough mix, by recirculation where appropriate.
4/- Always test for residual chlorine levels. It is desirable to leave a residual chlorine level of 0.3-0.5 mg/l after 30 minutes contact.
5/- During outbreaks it is recommended that chlorine residuals should be maintained as follow:
0.5 mg/l at all points in the supply
1.0 mg/l at standposts and wells
2.0 mg/l in tanker trucks at filling

(expected): 3 years (Unopened container)

Sales Text:
General Description: RETINOL
Vitamin A capsules, retinol (as palmitate) 200,000 units.
Pack of 500 capsules.

Uses:
Prevention and treatment of vitamin A deficiency.
Prevention of complications of measles.

Precautions:
Pregnancy; breastfeeding.

Dosage:
Prevention of vitamin A deficiency (universal or targeted distribution programmes), by mouth.
INFANTS less than 6 months: 50,000 units before 6 weeks of age, followed by 2 further doses of 50,000 units at intervals of 1 month (total dose 150,000 units).
INFANTS 6 to 12 months: 100,000 units, preferably at measles vaccination.
CHILD over 1 year (preschool): 200,000 units every 4 to 6 months.
ADULTS women of childbearing age or pregnant: maximum of 10,000 units daily or maximum 25,000 units weekly.
ADULTS in high-risk regions, mothers at or soon after delivery: 200,000 units, then further dose within 6 weeks.

Treatment of xerophthalmia, by mouth.
INFANTS less than 6 months: 50,000 units on diagnosis, repeated the next day and then after 2 weeks.
INFANTS 6 to 12 months: 100,000 units immediately on diagnosis, repeated the next day and then after 2 weeks.
CHILD over one year and ADULT (except women of child-bearing age): 200 ,000 units on diagnosis, repeated the next day and then after 2 weeks.
ADULT women of child-bearing age; severe signs of xerophthalmia, as for other adults; less severe cases (for example, night blindness): 5,000 to 10,000 units daily for at least 4 weeks or up to 25,000 units weekly.

Adverse Effects:
No serious or irreversible adverse effects in recommended doses. High levels may cause birth defects. Transient increased intracranial pressure in adults or a tense and bulging fontanelle in infants (with high dosage).
Massive overdose can cause rough skin, dry hair, an enlarged liver, a raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate, raised serum calcium and raised serum alkaline phosphatase concentrations.

NeisVac-C 0.5 ml suspension for injection in pre-filled syringe
Meningococcal group C polysaccharide conjugate vaccine adsorbed

Technical specifications:
One dose (0.5 ml) contains:
Neisseria meningitidis group C (strain C11) polysaccharide (de-O-acetylated)...10 micrograms
conjugated to tetanus toxoid............................................ ................................10-20 micrograms
adsorbed on aluminium hydroxide, hydrated...................................................0.5 mg Al3+

Indications:
Active immunisation of children from 2 months of age, adolescents and adults, for the prevention of invasive disease caused by Neisseria meningitidis serogroup C.

Pharmaceutical form
Suspension for injection in pre-filled syringe.
A semi-opaque white to off-white suspension.
Therapeutic indications
NeisVac-C is indicated for active immunisation in children from 2 months of age, adolescents and adults, for the prevention of invasive disease caused by Neisseria meningitidis serogroup C.
The use of NeisVac-C should be determined on the basis of official recommendations.
Method of administration
NeisVac-C is for intramuscular injection, preferably in the anterolateral thigh region in infants and the deltoid region in older children, adolescents, and adults. In children 12 to 24 months of age, the vaccine may be administered in the deltoid or the anterolateral thigh.
Shelf life:
See under storage and transportation

Storage and transportation:
Store in a refrigerator (2°C - 8°C). Do not freeze.
Keep the syringe in the outer carton in order to protect from light.
Within the indicated shelf life of 42 months the product may be stored at room temperature (up to +25°C) for a maximum single period of 9 months. During this period, the product may be returned to the refrigerator at 2-8°C. If stored at room temperature (up to +25°C) the starting date and the revised 9 months expiry date should be stated on the product package. The revised expiry date for storage at room temperature must not exceed the expiry date set in accordance with the total shelf life of 42 months.

Material safety data sheet information (MSDS):
Packaging and labeling:

NeisVac-C is presented as a 0.5 ml suspension in pre-filled syringe (type I glass) with a cap (bromobutyl rubber) and a plunger stopper (bromobutyl rubber) in packs of 1 or 10 or 20.
Each pre-filled syringe is packed in a blister. The opening in the blister seal is intended and allows for the equilibration of moisture during the recommended warm-up prior to the administration of the vaccine. Open the blister by removing the lid to take out the syringe. Do not press the syringe through the blister.
The pack of 1 may include up to two needles of different sizes. All needles are sterile and for single use only.
The primary packaging is latex-free.
Not all pack sizes may be marketed.
Upon storage, a white deposit and clear supernatant can be observed. The vaccine should be well shaken in order to obtain a homogeneous suspension and inspected for foreign particulate matter and discoloration prior to administration. Do not administer if particulate matter or discoloration is found and contact Pfizer Customer Service.
Any unused medicinal product or waste material should be disposed of in accordance with local requirements.
It is recommended to use the smaller one (0.50 x 16 mm) of the needles that may be included in the single packs for injection in children and the larger needle (0.60 x 25 mm) for vaccination in adults.

General Description:
Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, 13-valent.

Indications:
The vaccine is approved for active immunisation against disease caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae serotypes contained in the vaccine in infants and children from two months up to five years of age. Serious diseases that are often caused by pneumococci include pneumonia, meningitis and febrile bacteraemia; otitis media, sinusitis and bronchitis are more common but less serious manifestations of infection.

Administration:
The vaccine should be given by intramuscular injection. The preferred sites are anterolateral aspect of the thigh (vastus lateralis muscle) in infants or the deltoid muscle of the upper arm in young children.

Immunization Schedule:
Trials in several developing countries have demonstrated the efficacy of a 3-dose schedule for infants without a subsequent booster dose.

A single catch-up dose may be given to previously unvaccinated children aged 12-24 months and to children aged 2-5 years who are at high risk.
In countries where mortality among children aged <5 years is >50/1,000 live births or where >50,000 children die annually it should be considered a priority to include this vaccine in the national immunization programme(1)
(1) WER, Nr. 12, 2007, 82 WHO Position Paper Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for childhood vaccination.

The vaccine can be administered simultaneously with other paediatric vaccines in accordance with the recommended immunisation shedules. Different injectable vaccines should always be given at different injection sites.

General Description:
PREVENAR - Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, 13-valent

PREVENAR 13 (pneumococcal 13-valent conjugate vaccine) is a sterile suspension. The vaccine is composed of saccharides of the capsular antigen of Streptococcus pneumonia (S. pneumoniae), serotypes 1, 3, 4, 5, 6A, 6B, 7F, 9V, 14, 18C, 19A, 19F, and 23F, individually conjugated to diphtheria CRM197 protein, a nontoxic variant of diphtheria toxin.
PREVENAR 13 is manufactured as a liquid preparation. After shaking, the vaccine is a homogenous, white suspension.

COMPOSITION Paediatric Dose
Volume per dose 0.5 mL
Pneumococcal polysaccharide for serotypes
1, 3, 4, 5, 6A, 7F, 9V, 14, 18C, 19A, 19F & 23F 2.2 g of each
Pneumococcal polysaccharide for serotype 6B 4.4 g
Diphtheria protein CRM197 ~34 g
Aluminum as aluminum phosphate adjuvant 0.125 mg
Other ingredients:
Polysorbate 80
Sodium chloride
Water-for-injection

ADMINISTRATION
Shake well before use to homogenize the suspension, and only use if the vaccine is a homogenous, white suspension. Use a sterile syringe and a sterile needle for each injection.
The dose is 0.5 mL given intramuscularly, with care to avoid injection into or near nerves and blood vessels. The preferred sites are the anterolateral aspect of the thigh in infants or the deltoid muscle of the upper arm in older children and adults. The vaccine should not be injected in the gluteal area.

IMMUNIZATION SCHEDULE
Active immunization of infants and children from 6 weeks through 5 years of age against invasive disease, pneumonia and otitis media caused by S. pneumoniae serotypes 1, 3, 4, 5, 6A, 6B, 7F, 9V, 14, 18C, 19A, 19F and 23F.
Active immunization of adults, 50 years and older, against pneumonia and invasive disease caused by S. pneumoniae serotypes 1, 3, 4, 5, 6A, 6B, 7F, 9V, 14, 18C, 19A, 19F and 23F.

Infants and Children
PREVENAR 13 may be given at the same time as diphtheria, tetanus, acellular or whole-cell pertussis, Haemophilus influenzae type b, inactivated poliomyelitis, hepatitis B, meningococcal serogroup C, measles, mumps, rubella and varicella vaccines. When rotavirus or hepatitis A vaccines were given with PREVENAR 13, the safety profiles were similar, but immunogenicity was not measured.
The use of PREVENAR 13 should be based on official recommendations, taking into consideration the impact of invasive disease in different age groups, as well as variability of serotype epidemiology in different geographical areas.

Primary Immunization
For infants, the immunization series of PREVENAR 13 consists of three primary doses of 0.5 mL each. The first dose may be given as early as 6 weeks of age, with a minimum of 4 weeks between doses. A fourth, booster dose is recommended after the first birthday.
Alternatively, when PREVENAR 13 is given as part of a routine infant immunization programme, a three-dose schedule may be considered. The first dose may be given from the age of 2 months, with a second dose 2 months later, and a third (booster) dose is recommended between 11-15 months of age.
PREVENAR 13 may be given to infants with sickle cell disease or HIV infection.

For Previously Unvaccinated Older Children
For previously unvaccinated, older infants and children who are beyond the age of routine infant immunization, other schedules are recommended:
·Infants 7 to 11 months of age at first dose: three doses total (two doses at least 4 weeks apart, third dose after the first birthday and at least 2 months after the second dose)
·Children 12 to 23 months of age at first dose: two doses at least 2 months apart
·Children 24 months through 5 years of age at first dose: one dose
Alternatively, when PREVENAR 13 is routinely given as part of a generalized infant immunization programme, a single dose may be considered in previously unvaccinated children aged 12 to 23 months.

For Children Previously Vaccinated with PREVENAR
PREVENAR 13 contains the same 7 serotypes contained in pneumococcal 7-valent conjugate vaccine and is manufactured based on the same conjugate technology, using the same carrier protein CRM197. Children who have begun immunization with pneumococcal 7-valent conjugate vaccine may complete immunization by switching to PREVENAR 13 at any point in the schedule. In clinical trials, immunogenicity and safety profiles were comparable. A single dose of PREVENAR 13 in children 12-59 months of
age has been shown to induce immunity to the six additional serotypes.

Adults aged 50 years and older
One single dose.
The need for revaccination with a subsequent dose of PREVENAR 13 has not been established. Regardless of prior pneumococcal vaccination status, if the use of 23-valent polysaccharide vaccine is considered appropriate, PREVENAR 13 should be given first.

SIDE EFFECTS
Infants and Children
The most frequently reported adverse reactions included injection sitereaction, fever (
≥ 39ºC), irritability, drowsiness, restless sleep, decreased appetite, vomiting, diarrhea, and rash. Risks are associated with all vaccines.
Adults 50 years and older
The most frequently reported adverse reactions included pain at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, joint pain, decreased appetite, injection site redness, injection site swelling, limitation of arm movement, chills and rash.
PREVENAR 13 does not provide 100% protection against vaccine serotypes or protect against non-vaccine serotypes.

CONTRAINDICATIONS
Hypersensitivity to any component of the vaccine, including diphtheria toxoid.

STORAGE
Transport and store refrigerated at +2ºC to +8ºC.
DO NOT FREEZE. Discard if the vaccine has been frozen.

PRESENTATION
Vial, 1 Dose (50 per package)
Vial, 1 Dose (25 per package)

Vaccine Vial Monitors (VVMs) have been applied to the flip cap on all PREVENAR 13 Single Dose Vials manufactured by Wyeth Pharmaceuticals Inc. The colour dot which appears on the flip cap of the vial is the VVM. This is a time-temperature sensitive dot that provides an indication of the cumulative heat to which the vial has been exposed. It warns the end user when exposure to heat is likely to have degraded the vaccine beyond
an acceptable level.
The interpretation of the VVM is simple. Focus on the central square. Its colour willchange progressively. As long as the colour of this square is lighter than the colour of thering, then the vaccine can be used. As soon as the colour of the central square is the same colour as the ring or of a darker colour than the ring, then the vial should be discarded.

Multiple Micronutrient Powder, single-use 1 gram sachets, pack of 30
sachets in customised/country specific layouts;
MNPs are designed for point of use fortification of complementary foods for children and vulnerable populations to address anaemia and vitamin and mineral deficiencies.

Indications:
Micronutrient supplementation/food fortification in emergencies;
Micronutrient supplementation/food fortification in complementary foods for breast-fed infants.
Micronutrient supplementation/food fortification for young children where dietary micronutrient intakes are insufficient.

Target Group
Multiple micronutrient powder is used for children 6-59 months of age
Primary target: 6-24 months.

Technical Specifications

Composition per one gram sachet

Vitamin A 400µg (as dry CWS vitamin A acetate or palmitate beadlets)
Vitamin C 30mg (as ascorbic acid or sodium ascorbate)
Vitamin D 5µg (200IU) (as dry CWS Cholecalciferol)
Vitamin E 5mg TE (as CWS d or dl-alpha tocopheryl acetate)
Vitamin B1 0.5mg (as Thiamine mononitrate)
Vitamin B2 0.5.mg (Riboflavin or riboflavin -5-phosphate)
Vitamin B3 6mg (as Nicotinamide)
Vitamin B6 0.5mg (as Pyridoxine hydrochloride)
Vitamin B12 0.9µg (1% or 0.1% Cyanocobalamin on a carrier)
Folic acid 90µg
Iron 10mg (as coated Ferrous fumarate, Ferric pyrophosphate, NaFe EDTA*or Ferrous bisglycinate)
Zinc 4.1mg (as Zinc sulphate, oxide or gluconate)
Copper 0.56mg (as Copper gluconate or sulphate)
Selenium 17µg (as Sodium selenate or selenite or selenomethionine)

*Max 2.5mg of elemental iron from NaFeEDTA, the remaining 7.5mg of iron shall be added from another approved form.

Physical and organoleptic characteristics
Fine, off white, slightly yellow, speckled, odorless powder; having a bland taste which has minimal impact on the taste, smell or color of the food when mixed. The formulation shall be a stable, dry preparation that can be uniformly blended with the food the child is eating.

Consumer Guidance Messages:
Breastfeeding is recommended for 24 months and exclusively for 6 months.
Do not use if the sachet or package is torn or damaged.

Labelling
Customer to provide layouts for primary and secondary packaging.

Shelf life:
24 months

Storage conditions:
Dry ambient conditions. Store in a cool dry place, below 30 ºC

Instruction for use:
Mix the sachet contents with a small portion of solid or semi-solid food just before serving.

Children 6 to 59 months of age.

General Description:
Multiple Micronutrient Powder, single-use 1 gram sachets, pack of 30

Micronutrient supplementation/food fortification in complementary foods for breast-fed infants.
